thread:
marta: noticing some weird routing today — canary is getting ~40-50% of traffic even though rollout is 5% :thinking_face:
alex: wait what? did the split config change?
marta: no, config is still 5% in the console. saw it in dashboards: per-route token count shows ~5% but per-session sticky bucket shows canary-heavy
jen: any chance cookie path normalization is different between old/main and canary? we changed cookie code last week
kevin: possible. also remember the header-based routing fallback we added for region->x-region. could be header hash colliding with cookie hashing.
marta: i grabbed a few raw logs. small sample:```
[2026-01-18T14:12:01Z] request id=abc123 route=/v1/generate cookie=session=eyJ...; Path=/api; host=api.redwood.ai x-region=us-west
[2026-01-18T14:12:01Z] routed to=canary-2026-01-17 reason=sticky_cookie
```
alex: ah Path=/api — our sticky cookie key was using request.path when computing bucket hash. some clients send cookies scoped to / instead of /api, and code normalizes differently across proxies.
jen: do we have reproducer?
marta: yes, simple curl: `curl -H "Cookie: session=...; Path=/" -H "X-Region: us-west" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate` returns canary for me 7/10 times locally when split=5%
kevin: maybe the heuristic that chooses between cookie-hash vs header-hash is racy: iirc we prefer cookie if present, else header. but if cookie path mismatches we still compute hash against request.path, producing different hash for same logical user between frontend and routing service.
alex: posting current rollout config:```yaml
rollout:
  id: r-615
  strategy: traffic-split
  splits:
    - variant: main
      weight: 95
    - variant: canary-2026-01-17
      weight: 5
sticky:
  method: cookie
  cookie_name: rw_rollout
  cookie_scope: auto
```
kevin: deploy-bot just showed the canary image updated yesterday — maybe that change introduced path normalization differences between nginx sidecar and runtime.
deploy-bot: canary-2026-01-17 deployed by ci-pipeline at 2026-01-17T21:03:12Z :rocket:
jen: we should add metrics: count by (cookie_scope, cookie_path, route) to see correlation. also add a small unit test to canonicalize cookie path before hashing.
alex: quick mitigation: revert sticky preference so header-based hashing wins until we patch? or flip canary weight to 0 while investigating.
marta: on the dashboards I see that requests with cookie path "/" are landing on canary disproportionately. Flipping to header-first reduced canary to ~6% in staging.
kevin: plan: 1) flip heuristic in prod to header-first (rollbackable), 2) add path-canonicalization in routing lib + unit test, 3) add telemetry counters and an integration test that runs curl variants (Path=/, Path=/api) against rollout harness.
jen: estimate: 1) flip heuristic = 10m change + quick deploy, 2) canonicalization + tests = ~2 dev days, 3) telemetry + integ test = 1 dev day.
alex: i'll own the prod flip now, marta can run post-flip checks and revert if noisy.
marta: on it, starting flip now :eyes:
ci-bot: started job "canary-heuristic-flip/infra-deploy" (build 3821)
kevin: once flipped, let's schedule a postmortem note in incidents/ for visibility and add an e2e for cookie-scoped clients (mobile webview etc).
marta: flip done, monitoring: canary down to 5.8% in the first 2m. will watch 15m window.
jen: nice, open PR with the canonicalization and tests and link it here when ready.
alex: and add a tiny dashboard alert to warn when per-session split deviates >10% from configured split for 3m.
kevin: agreed. also, add note about cookie path normalization to rollout docs.
marta: creating a short post in #incidents with summary + timeline after 30m if stable. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
